<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **5** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3462dcf1f58d54f66ed1752b5b706d7181363631` — the merge of head `1965e42bf01f2a9f748f54dd7f4d47c4d6d34098` into base `7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3462dcf1f58d54f66ed1752b5b706d7181363631 && git checkout 3462dcf1f58d54f66ed1752b5b706d7181363631
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a 1965e42bf01f2a9f748f54dd7f4d47c4d6d34098 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a && git merge --no-ff 1965e42bf01f2a9f748f54dd7f4d47c4d6d34098

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Seat check

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-C) at head `a555ecc514b54c95ce7c725e120f77763b0e083f`, read 2026-11-20T09:14Z. This covers the T1 stale-prose batch for #35409, #34611 and #35522.

- **One L2 is owed:** CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, for the `packages/spec/src/**` face, which includes the N3 refusal string and the upgrade-guide entry. d7-C has started it. This ACCEPT does not replace it.
- **Condition:** CI at this head finishes green, except `Check Changeset`. That run is red only on the DELIBERATE CORRECTION below: I read its log, and the sole `##[error]` names `.changeset/35394-context-token-temporal-door.md` under #17712. When I read, 15 runs were `success`, 9 `skipped` and 41 in progress.

### DELIBERATE CORRECTION: `.changeset/35394-context-token-temporal-door.md`

- **Before:** "a scope that compares a `date` or `datetime` field with a context placeholder is now refused at compile".
- **After:** "a scope that compares a `date`, `datetime` or `time` field with a context placeholder is now refused at compile".

The correction is true. In `isUninterpretableTemporalComparand` (`temporal-comparand.ts`), a `context` placeholder is `judged-as-written` in `PLACEHOLDER_AT_THE_TEMPORAL_RULE`. It falls through to the kind's rule on all three kinds, and on `time` `readsAsWallClock` / `readsAsInstant` read no id. The same note's own subject and BREAKING line already name `date, datetime or time`, so the bullet was the one sentence out of step.

I confirm it here sentence by sentence. **But this is not the confirming record.** The diff changes runtime strings (the N3 refusal and the junk-literal consequence), not only release text or comments. So by landing-operations.md the confirming record is the same-head at-tier L2 PASS, which must judge this rewritten sentence. Please ask the reviewer to name it.

**Landing order.** Version Packages #35129 consumes this file. If #35129 lands first, the file is gone and this hunk conflicts. Then drop the hunk, and the shipped CHANGELOG keeps "date or datetime". In that case the same correction belongs in a follow-up note, which I'd leave to the seat. ⛔ Nothing here touches #35129.

### Runtime strings (both pinned, codes unchanged)

- **N3** (`record-currency-path.ts`). For a `currency` child the defect now names what `currencyConfig` lacks: `fixed` with no `defaultCurrency`, or a mode outside the three. A non-currency child keeps `kind`.
  - This arm is reached only after the `record` and well-formed `fixed` arms, and after a `dynamic` currency is admitted earlier, so the two words cover every currency child that reaches it.
  - The new spec pin asserts both phrasings.
  - "two predicates" → "three" in the module header: the module now exports a third.
- **Junk consequence** (`temporal-comparand-door.ts:747-749`). "compare false for EVERY row … indistinguishable from 'there is no data'" becomes "be compared as text, selecting every row or none, a 200 indistinguishable from a real answer".
  - This matches #35522's Done-when word for word, and d7-C's ruling A to keep it is right.
  - A positive pin on the junk cells was added. The two `not.toContain` pins on the misread and year classes now name the new phrase, so neither is vacuous.

### Prose, sentence by sentence

- **Per-kind placeholder rule.** The text in `temporal-comparand-door.ts`, `engine-top-level.ts`, `filter-normalizer.ts`, `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, `filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts`, `import-coerce.ts` and the lint RLS doc each matches the table above.
  - Date macro: stepped around, then judged by year (#20844).
  - Period key and context token: judged as written.
  - Unknown and record-context: left to the resolver (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`).
  - The lint doc's no-caller order is right: field-aware doors first, then the number door refuses every placeholder, then the resolver.
- **`$nin` const arm** (#34611, two places). They now say that inside a `$not` the lowering takes the NULL escape, or for a mixed spec a `$null: false` `set` leaf. The two places agree with each other.
- **`dashboards.mdx`.**
  - "usually runs inside the same statement" holds.
  - The ids-first reasons (other datasource, federated, middleware / `afterFind`, different driver options) are the semi-join decline reasons, and the list defers to Query Syntax for the full set.
  - "On a driver that compiles no subquery … a condition through a single-valued relation is refused before anything is read (`400 INVALID_FILTER`)" matches `relationReadDriverRefusal`: read verbs only, the first `!site.multiple` site, when `driverCompilesReadableIdsLeaf` is false.
- **Upgrade-guide entry and UI comments** (#35409). Each states the admitted set as "a `currency` field in `dynamic` mode, a stored home amount included". That matches #35409's Done-when and #35045's widening. The acceptance criterion's refused examples (`fixed` EUR, plain number, formula) are each outside that set.
- **Changeset.** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold: no accept set, key or code moves. The six `patch` bumps match the touched packages, and the two message changes are quoted FROM and TO.

### Nit (not owed)

`dashboards.mdx` no longer says what a multi-valued relation does on MongoDB, which is ids first under the cap. That case is now implied only by "single-valued". A clause ("a multi-valued one reads its ids first, as above") would close it.

### Unfiled finding: placeholder "to an id or a date"

File it as a p3 T1 rider for the next stale-prose batch. Do not widen this head while its L2 runs.

`engine-top-level.ts:965-966` and the number door's `FORM_SENTENCE.placeholder` (`filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts:521`) say a placeholder "resolves to an id or a date". This PR's own spec docblock now lists the ISO week key (`2026-W47`) as well. The runtime sentence is what a builder reads on the refusal, and it is incomplete rather than wrong, because a week key is not a number either. That is a weak but real business case, best carried by a batch rather than alone.

### Gates and routing

After the at-tier L2 PASS on `a555ecc5` (which also names the 35394 correction) and CI green apart from `Check Changeset`, the SKILL.md three conditions for landing red-with-correction apply, and `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35806` decides the route.

Check-runs on the head when read: 24 success, 9 skipped, 33 in progress, 1 failure (`Check Changeset`, see ③).

Result: PASS. No must-fix. Open on this head: S1, S2, S3, S4 (should-fix), N1 to N6 (nits).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`recordCurrencyDynamicRollupNotHomeError` (exported by `@objectstack/spec/data`): the words of one arm move, nothing else.** The new `defect` branch (`record-currency-path.ts:261-270`) is read only in the fallback arm (`:282`). The signature, the arm order and which children are refused are unchanged; a non-`currency` child still gets `kind`, so the four existing pins hold. Through both doors (`stack.zod.ts:5033`, `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`) the arm is reached only after `isTenantCurrencyAmount` answered false, so a `currency` child there has a mode that is not `dynamic`, not `record`, and not `fixed` with a string code. The two phrasings cover that set. Right. Edges that are not exactly covered: N2.
2. **The temporal door's junk refusal (`temporal-comparand-door.ts:745-749`): the consequence tail moves, the verdict does not.** Code `INVALID_FILTER`, status 400, the leading sentence, the remedy and "NOT applied" are unchanged. Lint's `refusalVerdict` quotes the leading sentence, so no finding text moves. The new tail is truer than the old one and still not exactly true: S1.
3. **No `.describe()` and no schema TSDoc changed.** The spec hunks are a module header, a function body, a second module header and a migration entry's strings. `content/docs/references/**` is untouched and nothing in it holds any changed sentence (`git grep` on the head). No regeneration was owed and none was done. Right. `check:docs`, `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` sit in `Type Check`, which was still in progress when read.
4. **No export, key, accepted value, default or code moves.** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right (②).
5. **Sentence by sentence, against the head:**

| Sentence | Verdict |
|:---|:---|

'dynamic') === 'dynamic'`, and `isStoredHomeField` requires the same two, so a stored home amount is a member. |

| Entry 18 `reason`, "`defineStack` admitted it only there" | False as history: S3. |
| Per-kind placeholder rule (`temporal-comparand-door.ts:93-104` and `:197`, `engine-top-level.ts:954-958`, `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:1179-1183` and `:1449-1454`, `import-coerce.ts:350-354`, `filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts:181-187`) | True against `PLACEHOLDER_AT_THE_TEMPORAL_RULE` (`core/src/utils/temporal-comparand.ts:292-298`, applied at `:364-365`) and `judgeResolvedToken` (date macros only, year only). `having` asks the same predicate. |
| `filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts:185-187`, resolved forms now include the ISO week key | True (`PERIOD_KEY_RESOLVERS`). It now disagrees with the runtime sentence in the same file: S4. |
| `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts:205-214`, which answer a placeholder gets with no caller | False for a boolean field: S2. |
| `filter-normalizer.ts:628-640` and `:2511-2516`, the `$nin` reasoning | True against `guardNullPolarity` (`filter-lowering.ts:445-470`): outside a `$not` every `$nin` is wrapped in `nullEscape`; inside one, `allowNull` takes the escape and `requireValue` takes `{ f: { $null: false } }` unless `requiredFields` already holds the field. Tried and held: an authored escape, a double `$not`, an `$or` arm under `$not`, a spec beside an enclosing `$and` requirement. The parenthetical is short: N5. |
| `dashboards.mdx:580-591` | Agrees with `query-syntax.mdx:709-732` and with `relationReadDriverRefusal` (`relation-filter-lowering.ts:356-381`): `aggregate` is in `SEMI_JOIN_READ_VERBS`, the first single-valued site is refused before any related read, and the analytics engine path hands the condition to the engine's `where`. Two loose ends: N1. |
| Junk consequence, `temporal-comparand-door.ts:747-749` | Not exactly true: S1. |
| `.changeset/35394-context-token-temporal-door.md:25` | True: see ③. |

### ② Semver level

- **Levels.** Six `patch` bumps: right. The kind is `none` and `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/objectql` each ship a changed runtime string, so a changeset is owed there. The other four ship comments or docblocks only; bumping them is harmless: N6.
- **Does a changed refusal message count as a contract change?** Not under this repo's clause. `Clause-②` covers what is accepted or exported, and `Metadata-protocol` what an author can write; neither moves. The stable half of a refusal is its code and status, both unchanged (`INVALID_METADATA` / 422, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400). In-repo matchers on either old text: none outside the tests this diff updates (`git grep` on the head for "compare false for EVERY row" and for the `currency`-child fallback words). The precedent agrees: `.changeset/35045-dynamic-summary-tenant-child.md` records a refusal's reworded head as prose under its own declarations. A consumer outside the repo who matches on message text gets the FROM and TO in the changeset, which quotes both. Sufficient.
- **`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.** Right, on the claim, the PR body and the changeset body, each line-initial.
- **FROM/TO.** Present for both messages. The first bullet is looser than the code (N2). The second quotes the new sentence, so it inherits S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/35394-context-token-temporal-door.md`: judged here, and confirmed.**
  - Before: "a scope that compares a `date` or `datetime` field with a context placeholder is now refused at compile, `READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED` (500, fail-closed)."
  - After: "a scope that compares a `date`, `datetime` or `time` field with a context placeholder is now refused at compile, `READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED` (500, fail-closed)."
  - Verdict: the rewritten sentence is true. A `context` placeholder is `judged-as-written` on every kind; on `time` it falls to `!(readsAsWallClock(s) || (readsAsInstant(s) && keepsTimeOfDay(s)))`, which is true for `{current_user_id}`. The analytics admission asks `IObjectQLEngine.judgeFilter`, which runs that door (`judgeWhereAdmission` calls `lowerWhereFilterArray`). The `time` cell is pinned in core (`temporal-comparand.test.ts`, the #35394 block loops `date`, `datetime`, `time`). The same note's title, BREAKING line and TO line already say all three kinds, so this bullet was the one sentence out of step. Nothing else in the note is touched; its frontmatter (`@objectstack/core: patch`) is unchanged.
  - Is the edit allowed? Yes. The note is still pending on the merge base, the correction is asked for by this PR's own card (#35522, comment 7013425050, N6), and it is declared in the PR body by file name with the corrected sentence quoted. The class as `check-empty-changeset.mjs` describes it is a PR that falsified a pending note; here the note was incomplete from the start and this PR changes no behaviour it describes. The gate cannot tell the shapes apart and the remedy is the same, so the declaration is the right one.
  - This record is the same-head at-tier record that `landing-operations.md` names for a diff that also changes code.
- **`Check Changeset` is red by design.** Its log on this head carries one refusal, naming `.changeset/35394-context-token-temporal-door.md` under #17712, and no other error. Accepted: restoring the file from the base would put the incomplete sentence back, and `skip-changeset` is forbidden. Every other check must still finish green; 33 were in progress when read.
- **Landing order against Version Packages #35129.** #35129 consumes the pending note. If it lands first, the file is gone and this hunk conflicts. Then drop the hunk. The shipped CHANGELOG entry keeps "`date` or `datetime`", and the correction goes where AGENTS.md puts it: an amendment of that released entry in a dedicated docs-only PR. ⛔ Not a later note: the L1 ACCEPT says "a follow-up note", which the Documentation Guardrails row for `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` forbids. A rebase gives a new head, and this record covers `a555ecc5` only.
- **Open question in the os-dev-report (the junk sentence is a second runtime string, outside the PM note).** Option A was taken. Accepted: #35522's Done-when names that sentence, and the pins moved with it. The wording itself is S1.
- **File surface.** The claim names `packages/objectql/src/validation/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts`; the file is `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts`, and `@objectstack/lint` is in the changeset. Accepted. `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` gets two comments where the card's addition names one; the second is the same sentence on `having`. Accepted.
- **#34611 N2 (the #34514 changeset sentence) left as it is.** Accepted: the note is released (`packages/services/service-analytics/CHANGELOG.md`), and the card says to fix only the docs in that case.
- **Skills text** (`skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md:182-185` still says the build refuses `dynamic` on any other roll-up). Out of scope by the card; seat 5 files it. Not held against this PR.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

**Are the pins real?**

| Pin | Result |
|:---|:---|
| N3, `currency-summary-home-rollup.test.ts:358-369` | Real. Each arm is asserted by its own substring, so dropping `defect` or swapping the arms goes red; the report's ablation shows the first. Function level only: no door-level case hands such a child to the arm, and the non-string mode rendering is not pinned (N2). |
| Junk phrase, `engine-temporal-comparand-door.test.ts:202` | Real: `toContain` on four junk comparands through `engine.find`. A reworded sentence goes red. |
| The two `not.toContain` pins (`engine-temporal-comparand-door.test.ts:453`, `engine-temporal-year-range.test.ts:229`) | Live only because the positive pin anchors the phrase. Fixing S1 moves all three together. |
| Comments, docblocks, docs, entry 18, changesets | No pin and none possible; they stand on this reading. |

**Is patch right, and is anything owed that was not shipped?** Patch is right and nothing generated is owed (①.3, ②).

**The unfiled finding ("resolves to an id or a date").** A follow-up, not a must-fix here: S4.

S1 (should-fix) — the new junk consequence is still wrong for part of its class. `packages/objectql/src/temporal-comparand-door.ts:747-749` says "it would reach the driver and be compared as text, selecting every row or none, a 200 indistinguishable from a real answer."

- "every row or none" is absolute. On a `date` field the junk class holds every string with no leading real `YYYY-MM-DD` (`misreadClassOf` returns `undefined` for a `date` hit that is not an impossible day). `{ placed_on: { $gte: '2026' } }` and `{ $gte: '2026-06' }` are such strings. Compared as text against stored `YYYY-MM-DD` values they select the rows from 2026 on, or from June 2026 on: a subset. `'2026/07/15'` splits the rows too.
- "a 200" does not hold on PostgreSQL. The same file's measurements record text handed to a `date` column as "200 [] on memory and SQLite, 500 on PostgreSQL" (`:144`), and the year-class comment a few lines up says "or, on PostgreSQL, a database error" (`:723`). The misread sentences already say "the wrong rows or a database error".

The card's Done-when says "may select every row or none", and the `having` twin (`:827-828`) has the same shape, which is why this is not a must-fix. Fix: "As written it would reach the driver and be compared as text: it may select every row, none or the wrong ones (or raise a database error), an answer indistinguishable from a real one." Move the pinned substring in the three tests and the quoted sentence in `.changeset/t1-stale-prose.md:18` with it, and give `:827-828` the same words.

S2 (should-fix) — the lint docblock's decision order leaves out the boolean arm. `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts:207-213` says the field-aware doors answer on a temporal field and on a number field, and "Otherwise the resolver answers". On a `boolean` field every placeholder is refused before the resolver too: `narrowNumberComparands` carries the #21333 boolean arm (`engine-top-level.ts`, the comment under the number door), and `filter-boolean-comparand-declared-type.ts:234` answers `placeholder` for any `classifyFilterToken` hit. So `record.is_open == '{current_user_id}'` answers `INVALID_FILTER`, where the sentence says `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`. The L1 ACCEPT calls this order right; it is one arm short.
